"And his saying, upon him be blessings and peace, in the hadith: 'He passed His hand over the back of Adam'" may allow that the one who passed the hand is the angel appointed over the shaping of embryos, their creation, and the gathering of their materials, and it is ascribed to God, Exalted is He, because He is the One who commands, just as the causing to die is ascribed to Him in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿God takes the souls at the time of their death﴾, while the one who takes them is the angel, according to His saying, Exalted is He: (the angels take them). It may also be that the one who passed the hand is God, Exalted is He, and the passing of the hand is from the mode of figurative expression. It was said: it is from "measurement" (misaha), in the sense of determination, as if he said: He determined what was in his back of offspring. End of his words. Some of them said: The meaning in the hadith is not that He, Exalted is He, brought forth all of them from the back of Adam, peace be upon him, directly; rather, He brought forth from his back his biological sons, and from their backs their biological sons, and so on to the end of the chain. But since the original locus of appearance was his back, upon him be blessings and peace, and since the purpose of the hadith was to explain the state of the two groups in summary without the mention of intermediaries being a purpose, the bringing forth of all was attributed to him. As for the noble verse, since it was addressed as an argument against the disbelievers contemporary with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and to show that the excuse of ascribing their association to their fathers is of no benefit, the context required attributing the bringing forth of each one of them to the back of his father, without addressing the bringing forth of the biological sons of Adam from his back, which is certain. The absence of a statement of the covenant in the 'Umar report is not an explanation of its absence, nor does it necessitate it. End.

You know that the interpretation mentioned by al-Baydawi is utterly rejected by the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both; and what some have mentioned, that the context of the hadith is an summary explanation of the state of the two groups, is refuted by the evident fact that the question was not about their state, such that the hadith would be brought to explain it. For the apparent point is that the Companion asked him, upon him be blessings and peace, about what was unclear to him in the meaning of the verse: whether the making witness is literal or figurative? When he answered him, upon him be blessings and peace, with what made clear to him what he intended—since he was eloquent—and if something else had been unclear to him, it would have been obligatory to explain that aspect; and likewise al-Faruq, may God be pleased with him, understood it.

From here it is known that the statement of the Imam that the apparent meaning of the verse indicates the bringing forth of the offspring from the back of the children of Adam, and that there is nothing in it indicating that they were brought forth from the loins of Adam, nor anything indicating its negation, except that the report indicates it—so that it establishes their emergence from Adam by the hadith and from his sons by the verse—does not agree with the context of the hadith, as is not hidden. Shaykh Shihab al-Din al-Turbashti said: Many scholars have striven to flee from saying regarding the meaning of the verse what the apparent report of the Rabbi (habr) requires, because of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Lest you say on the Day of Resurrection: Indeed we were unaware of this﴾. So they said: If this acknowledgment was from compulsion, since they were uncovered to the reality of the matter and witnessed it with the certainty of sight, then they had the right on that Day to say: "We bear witness" on that day; but when the knowledge of necessity departed from us and we were left to our own opinions, some of us were right and some of us erred. And if it was from inference, but they were protected at that time from error, then they also have the right to say: We were supported on the day of the acknowledgment with success and protection, and we were deprived of both afterwards; and had we been continually supported with them, our testimony at every time would have been like our testimony on the first day. It is then necessary that by the covenant be meant what God, Exalted is He, placed in them of intellects and gave them of insights, because these are the conclusive proof and the preventer against their saying: "Indeed we were..." etc. Because God, Exalted is He, made the acknowledgment and the capacity to know His lordship and His oneness, glorified is He, a proof against them regarding association, just as He made the sending of the Messenger a proof against them regarding belief in what he reported of the unseen. End.

Its summary is that if the verse is not interpreted by what has been mentioned, it follows that they would not be made to be without argument on the Day of Resurrection. It has been answered by choosing each of the two alternatives and removing its difficulty. As for the first, it is said: when they say "We bear witness on that day," but when the knowledge of necessity departed and we were left to our own opinions, it was thus—O liars, when were you left to your own opinions? Did We not send Our messengers in succession to wake you from the custom of heedlessness? As for the second, it is said: this is a shared implication, for when it is said to them: Did We not grant you intellects and insights? They may say: then if we were deprived of grace and success, what benefit is there for us in intellect and insight? Muhyi al-Sunnah, in answer to the question of how the argument is binding when no one remembers that covenant, said that God, Exalted is He, made the proofs clear for His oneness and the truthfulness of His messengers regarding what they reported; so whoever denies it is obstinate, violating the covenant, and the argument binds him; and his forgetting it and his not retaining it does not nullify the argument after the report of the truthful informant. This is not free from difficulty. Therefore some answered that His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿that you say﴾ is not an object of His saying: ﴿and He made them bear witness﴾ and what branches from it of their saying ﴿"Yes, we bear witness"﴾, so that it would be necessary that this making witness and this testimony be preserved for them in their being held to account; rather, it is for an implied verb to which the speech extends, and the meaning is: We did what We did of the command to mention the covenant and its explanation, out of aversion that you say, O disbelievers, on the Day of Resurrection: "Indeed we were unaware of that covenant; we were not alerted to it in the abode of obligation, and had we been, we would have acted upon its requirement." This is according to the reading of the majority. As for the other reading, it is an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu) for the implied verb itself, which governs "when He took" (idh akhadha); and the meaning is: remind them of the covenant taken from them in the past, lest they excuse themselves on the Day of Resurrection by heedlessness of it or by imitating their fathers. Then he said: This is on the assumption that "We bear witness" is from the speech of the offspring, which is the apparent reading; but if it is from the speech of God, Exalted is He, then it governs "that you say," and there is no difficulty at all, and the meaning is: We bore witness to this saying of yours, lest you say on the Day of Resurrection, etc., because We will refute and reject you then. End.

It is not hidden that what he mentioned first, that "that" (an) and what follows it are linked to an implied verb to which the speech extends, or to the implied verb itself governing "when," is clearly sufficient to remove the difficulty we pointed to, and it is, by my life, extremely fine. However, the apparent reading is that it is linked to the making witness and what branches from it; and I see that the answer, while not departing from it, does not avoid departing from it. What supports what he mentioned second, that "We bear witness" is from the speech of God, Exalted is He, and that it is the governing element, is what Ibn 'Abd al-Barr reported in al-Tamhid through the chain of al-Suddi from Abu Malik, and from Abu Talib from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both; and from Murrah al-Hamdani from Ibn Mas'ud and some Companions that they said about the verse: When God brought Adam out of Paradise before his descent from heaven, He passed the right side of his back and brought forth from it offspring white like pearls, in the form of ants; and He said to them: Enter Paradise by My mercy. And He passed the left side of his back and brought forth from it offspring black like ants; and He said: Enter the Fire, and I do not mind. That is His saying: ﴿the companions of the right﴾ and ﴿the companions of the left﴾. Then He took from them the covenant, and said: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes." He gave a group willingly and a group unwillingly, by way of taqiyya; and he and the angels said: ﴿We bear witness, lest you say on the Day of Resurrection﴾, the hadith.

In it is a contradiction to what was reported from the Rabbi earlier, that the taking was at Nu'man, for that is apparent in that this was after the descent, and this is apparent in that it was before. And in some reports is what indicates that it was when His throne was upon the water.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 7, verse 173 (part 2 of 3):

Abd ibn Humayd, al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi in Nawadir al-Usul, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azamah, and Ibn Mardawayh have related from Abu Umamah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah Most High created the creation, decreed the decree, took the covenant of the Prophets, and His Throne was upon the water. He took the People of the Right with His right hand, and He took the People of the Left with His other hand, and both hands of the Merciful are right. He said: 'O People of the Right!' and they responded to Him, saying: 'At Your service, our Lord, and at Your bidding!' He said: 'Am I not your Lord?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'O People of the Left!' and they responded to Him, saying: 'At Your service, our Lord, and at Your bidding!' He said: 'Am I not your Lord?' They said: 'Yes.'"

Some have mixed some of these reports with others, the report continuing. Some mentioned that it took place in India, where Adam (peace be upon him) descended, and others that it took place at the site of the Ka'bah, and that the offspring brought forth from the loins of Adam (peace be upon him) were like particles that surrounded him, and they made the place they occupied at that time a sanctuary. There is no reliable chain of transmission upon which one may depend for this. Reconciling these narrations is difficult, except by saying that the taking of the covenant occurred more than once. This is the view of the Sufi masters, may Allah sanctify their secrets. However, their statements imply a difference in kind. Some of them have said: "I have seen someone recall, before the covenant of 'Am I not' (alast), six other covenantal stations." I mentioned that to our shaykh, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said: "If the speaker intends the six presences that he knew before the covenant of 'Am I not' in general, then it is granted. But if he intends the total of the covenantal presences that came before 'Am I not,'
page 106
then they are more than that." From this one learns what is in their saying: "No one remembers that covenant in an absolute, total negation of recollection." It is also related from Dhu al-Nun, when he was asked about it, whether he remembered it, that he said: "It is as if it were now in my ear." Some, offering it as a plausible view, said: "This covenant was yesterday, and in it he also pointed to other covenants that were before it." It may be said that their intention by that negative statement is: no one among the polytheists remembers that covenant, not: no one at all.

Qutb al-Haqq wa al-Din, the scholar al-Shirazi, in reconciling the verse with the report of 'Umar, offered a discussion that the eminent scholars accepted and received with approval. Its summary: the Prophet's answer (ﷺ), when he was asked about the verse, was of the type of the "style of the wise" (uslub al-hakim), for he (peace be upon him) was asked about the explanation of the present covenant and answered by explaining the spoken covenant in the most subtle manner.

Its explanation: Allah, glorified is He, had two covenants with the children of Adam. One of them is reached by reason through the establishment of proofs that move one to recognize the present covenant. The second is the spoken covenant, which reason does not reach by itself, but depends on the declaration of one who knows the states of the servants from eternity to eternity, such as the prophets (peace be upon them). So the Prophet (ﷺ) wished to teach the community and inform them that behind the covenant that they reach by their intellects there is another, eternal covenant. Thus he said what he said about wiping the back of Adam (peace be upon him) in eternity and bringing forth the offspring, so that it might be known from it that this progeny which keeps emerging from the loins of the children of Adam is the same particle that was brought forth in eternity from the loins of Adam and from which the eternal spoken covenant was taken, just as the present covenant, the ever-continuing, was taken from them gradually when they were brought forth. End of quotation. This is good, as they said, but the word "eternal" (azal) in it and "ever-continuing" (la yazal) should be understood figuratively, because the emergence of the progeny is limited by the Day of Resurrection. On the view that it does not cease after that, it is specific to the blessed in a particular manner, as is known in its proper place. The matter is originated, not eternal; otherwise it would entail breaching the consensus of the Muslims and a contradiction with the verse, and "Allah was, and there was nothing with Him."

It is reported from al-Khalkhali that he rolled up his sleeves to refute this and said: "Those addressed are the eternal knowledge-forms, which are the quiddities and realities of things, and they call them the fixed entities. Those forms do not exist in the external world, so no making (ja'l) is connected to them in accordance with that fixity. Rather, in their own essences they do not need anything to make them those forms, and they proceed from Him, Exalted, by the most holy outpouring. They have explicitly stated that they are modes and considerations of the Single Essence. Their answer to the objection is: 'Rather, it is by the tongues of their eternal preparedness (isti'dad), not by the tongues that come after their realization in the external world.'" End of quotation.

This rests on the distinction between fixed existence (thubut) and actual existence (wujud), and there is a long dispute about it, but we are among those who hold it, and Allah does not feel shy before the truth. From here an alternative reconciliation of the verse and the hadith has occurred to some excellent scholars: that what is meant by the offspring extracted from the loins of Adam and his sons are the knowledge-forms and the fixed entities; that the meaning of their extraction is the manifestation (tajalli) of the Single Essence and its appearance within them; that the attribution of extraction to their appearance is because those forms, when they come into existence in the external realm, become their very selves; and that that speaking is a preparedness-speech, eternal, not a spoken speech, not ever-continuing, originated. This is what the shaykh and gnostic Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami related in al-Haqa'iq from Banan, where he said: "He brought them into being before Him in an eternal state; then He called them, and they answered Him swiftly, and He made Himself known to them when they were not in human form; then He brought them forth by His will as creatures and deposited them in the loins of Adam." So He, glorified is He, said: "And when your Lord took..." etc. He thus informed that He addressed them while they did not exist except through His existence for them, since they possessed the Truth in their non-existence as selves, and the Truth was present with the Truth in that. Then al-Sulami recited for one of them:

"If they heard as I heard her speech, they would fall prostrate and bowing before 'Izzah."

It is not hidden that this reconciliation is far, by many stages, from the taste of the people of the outward meaning, for it contradicts the apparent sense of the reports and what is understood from the narrations. And what is reported from Banan, in it—and it is the beginning of his speech—"He chose them for guardianship and selected them for honour, and gave them broad scope in the deep hidden matters of the unseen kingdom," and after it what he mentioned; and its inclusion of all creation, the happy and the wretched, is not free from remoteness. The Greatest Shaykh, may his secret be sanctified, mentioned that Allah, Most High, originated the originated things and manifested Himself in the tongue of the Oneness within the Lordship, and said: "Am I not your Lord?" The one addressed was in complete attentiveness, so they said: "Yes" (bala). It was like an echo, for they answered Him with it, since the originated existence is a set-up illusion. This testimony was a testimony of mercy, for He, glorified is He, did not say to them "my own self" (wahdi), out of sparing them, since He knew that they would associate others with Him—exalted is He far above that by a great exaltation—because of the natural portion in them and because of their acceptance of divine power, and what He knows except a few. You know that the verifying exegetes regarded the oneness in the testimony and likewise in the witnessing, as the allusion to it has passed and the reports speak of it. Among that is what Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal related in the Zawa'id of the Musnad, al-Bayhaqi, Ibn 'Asakir, and a group, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that he said concerning the verse: "He gathered them all together, made them spirits in their forms, then made them speak, and they spoke; then He took from them the covenant and the pledge, and made them witness against themselves: 'Am I not your Lord?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'I call the seven heavens to witness against you, and I call your father Adam to witness against you, lest you say on the Day of Resurrection: We did not know of this. Know that there is no god but Me, and no lord but Me, and do not associate anything with Me. I shall send My messengers to you to remind you of My covenant and My pledge, and I shall send down My books upon you.' They said: 'We testify that You are our Lord and our God; we have no lord but You and no god but You.' So they acknowledged. And He raised Adam over them, looking at them, and he saw the rich and the poor, the handsome and those below that, and said: 'O Lord, why did You not make Your servants equal?' He said: 'I loved that I be thanked.'"

By this is dispelled what is said: that the acknowledgment of the offspring of His, glorified is He, lordship does not contradict polytheism, since the polytheists also profess His lordship, as His saying, Exalted, indicates: "And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, Allah." The Mu'tazilah deny the spoken covenant mentioned in the reports and say that it belongs to the solitary reports (ahad), so we are not obliged to abandon for it the apparent sense of the Book. They impugned its authenticity with rational premises built on philosophical principles, as is their habit in such matters. They first said: taking a covenant is possible only from a rational being; therefore a person must remember that covenant in this world, for it is not permissible for a rational being to forget such a great event with total forgetting. Since he forgets it thus, this shows it did not occur. By a similar argument the doctrine of metempsychosis (tanasukh) is refuted. It was answered that knowledge is only by the creation of Allah, Exalted, so He may not create it for a wisdom He knows; and the proof of the falsity of metempsychosis is not limited to what was mentioned. They have also argued against it from the necessity that the body would have two souls, as the Imam explained in al-Mabahith al-Sharqiyyah, and that the number of the dead would equal the number of the living, while the general epidemics contradict this equality. Moreover, it may be answered by distinguishing between metempsychosis and our case: when we are in other bodies and remain in them for years, it is customarily impossible for us to forget their conditions; but the taking of the covenant occurred in the briefest time, so forgetting in it is not far-fetched. Some answered that forgetting and non-remembrance here are due to the length of time; and it was objected that the people of the Hereafter know much of the affairs of this world, as the verses and reports attest. Unless it is said that this is a particularity of that abode. They said secondly: that progeny taken from the loins of Adam (peace be upon him) must each have a measure of structure so that knowledge and understanding may arise in it, so their totality cannot be contained by the expanse of this world; therefore their existence in the loins of Adam, to be taken and then returned, is impossible. It was answered that this is based on life being

page 108

...are conditioned by the specific bodily structure, as the opponents hold. The proof against this is established, as it has been settled in *kalam* (scholastic theology). So it is possible for God Most High to create life in an indivisible particle (*jawhar fard*). Those extracted descendants were like ants (*dharr*), and the ant is close to the particle. The claim that the whole collection cannot be contained in the expanse of this world is not granted. If the taking of the covenant occurred in heaven before Adam's descent (ﷺ), then the circle is wide. If it occurred when the Throne was upon the water, then the circle is wider. There is no obstacle, if it was on earth, for the gathering of the ants to be piled up between it and the sky, and that is indeed a vast space, even if its base is small. And if one considers that the human being is a reference to the rational soul (*al-nafs al-natiqah*), and that it is an immaterial substance that neither occupies space nor inheres in anything, then it does not need space. However, there is what there is.

Third, they said: there is no benefit in taking the covenant, because by it they do not become deserving of reward and punishment, and moreover they are in a lower state than children, and a child is not subject to obligation, so how can obligation be directed at the ants? (It is answered:) the benefit of the taking is not limited to the aforementioned deservingness. Rather, it may be to display the perfection of power to those present among the angels, and to establish proof on the Day of Resurrection, as the saying of some regarding the verse requires. As for their being at that time in a lower state than children, this is within the realm of nullity, as is not hidden from one who is in a lower state than children.

Fourth, they said: Glorious and Exalted is He said: ﴿And We created man from an extract of clay﴾, and He, Majestic and Exalted, said: ﴿So let man look at what he was created from. He was created from a gushing fluid﴾. And the fact that those ants are human beings contradicts the human being being created from these things.

It is answered: the human being in this present existence is created from that, and it does not follow that in that other mode of existence he is likewise, moreover God Most High is not incapable of anything. In sum, the believer should affirm that taking, for the reports that speak of it proceed from the source of prophethood. One should not heed the words of one who says that it is a practice abandoned because it rests on solitary reports (*ahad*), for that leads to closing a great door of divine unveilings, and deprives its speaker of great divine gifts. Al-Bayhaqi related in *al-Madkhal* from al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "All those we have met affirm a report from one to one to one, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and they make it a Sunnah. Whoever follows it is praised, and whoever opposes it is blamed." He also said: "Whoever opposes this doctrine is, in our view, one who has departed from the path of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the people of knowledge after them, and he is among the people of ignorance."

In *Jami' al-Usul* from Razin, from Abu Rafi', that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Let me not find any one of you whose matter comes to him from my command, whether I have commanded it or forbidden it, while he is reclining on his couch, saying, 'We do not know what this is; we have the Book of Allah, and this is not in it.'" The hadith continues.

It is not fitting to inquire into the mode of that, for it is among the sciences that are left unspoken, requiring the lifting of the veil and the outpouring of bounty.

Among this is what al-Jundi related in *Fada'il Makkah*, as did Abu al-Hasan al-Qattan, al-Hakim, and al-Bayhaqi in *Shu'ab al-Iman*, and he weakened it, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: "We performed Hajj with Umar, may Allah be pleased with him. When he entered the circumambulation he faced the Stone and said: 'I know that you are a stone that neither harms nor benefits. Had I not seen the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) kiss you, I would not kiss you.' Then he kissed it. Ali, may Allah ennoble his face, said to him: 'O Commander of the Faithful, it does harm and benefit.' He said: 'By what?' He said: 'By the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.' He said: 'And where is that in the Book of Allah?' He said: 'Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam...﴾ up to His words, Glorified is He: ﴿Yes﴾.' That is because Allah, Mighty is His affair, created Adam, peace be upon him, and wiped over his back, and brought forth his descendants. He made them acknowledge that He is the Lord and they are the servants, and He took their pledges and covenants, and wrote that in a scroll. This Stone had two eyes and a tongue. He said to it: 'Open your mouth,' and it opened its mouth, and he put that scroll into it, and said: 'Bear witness for whoever meets you with fidelity on the Day of Resurrection. And I bear witness, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say:'" [Page 109] "'The Black Stone will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and it will have an eloquent tongue to bear witness for whoever touches it with monotheism.' So it, O Commander of the Faithful, harms and benefits." Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I seek refuge in Allah that I should live among a people in which you are not present, O Abu al-Hasan."

It has been said: from here is known his saying (ﷺ): "The Stone is the right hand of Allah on His earth."

The discussion of this is well known. Here, some people have mentioned that after the people said "Yes," some of them prostrated twice, some did not prostrate at all, some prostrated the first prostration with the first group but not the second, and some did the reverse. The first category are those who live as believers and die likewise; the second are those who live as unbelievers or die so; the third are those who live as believers and die as unbelievers; the fourth are those who live as unbelievers or die as believers. End of quotation. This is a statement that neither the Book nor the Sunnah witnesses to, so it is not to be relied upon. Similar is the claim that some of those who said "Yes" were deceitful at that time, when Iblis appeared to them in that gathering, and they thought he was the one saying "Am I not your Lord?", so they answered him.

Those are the wretched, and some of them, the Lord, Glorified is He, manifested Himself to them, so they recognized Him and answered Him; those are the blessed. This, in my view, is utterly false. What should be believed is that they all directed the answer to the Lord of Lords. Indeed, some have held that some answered out of compulsion, and they cited some of the earlier reports for it. Those who hold this view maintain that the children of polytheists are in the Fire. Whoever says they are in Paradise holds that they acknowledged by choice at the taking of the covenant, and so they enter Paradise by that acknowledgment. And Allah, Glorified is He, is the Most Merciful of the merciful. As for attributing the speech in the verse, according to some opinions, to the plural pronoun, it is only by considering that it proceeded from some of them, for its proceeding from all of them is manifestly false, and the like of this occurs in the verses frequently.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 7, verse 174:

﴿Thus do We detail the verses﴾: That is, this eloquent detailing, which brings about great benefits, is what We set forth, and nothing else.

﴿So that perhaps they will return﴾: from their persistence in falsehood, We set forth this detailing. It was said: the meaning is, "So that perhaps they will return to the first covenant, remember it, and act in accordance with its requirements. We do this." In either case, the "wa" (and) is initial (ibtida'iyyah), as in the one before it. It is also permitted that it be coordinating (ataf) upon an implied clause, meaning: "So that they may understand what it contains of incentives and warnings," or "So that the truth may become manifest, and so that perhaps they will return." It was also said that it is the "sword of the orator" (saif khatib).

This (and by way of allusion, ishara) they said: ﴿And ask them about the town﴾, that is, about the people of the town of the body, who are the spirit, the heart, the commanding self (al-nafs al-ammarah), and its followers: ﴿which was by the sea﴾, that is, overlooking the shore of the sea of humanity.

﴿When they transgressed in the Sabbath﴾: they overstepped the limits of Allah the Exalted on the day when the enjoyment of some of the carnal pleasures is forbidden to them. The transgressor among those people is none other than the commanding self, for it, in the seasons of acts of obedience and of restraint from desires, such as the month of Ramadan for example, is eager to partake of what it has been forbidden, and a person is eager for what is forbidden to him.

﴿When their fish came to them﴾, and these are the matters from which they were forbidden to partake, ﴿on their Sabbath day﴾, the day which they were commanded to honor by law, ﴿close at hand (qariban) in its approach﴾; ﴿and on the day they did not keep the Sabbath, they did not come﴾, in that there is not made ready for them what they desire.

﴿Thus We test them﴾: We deal with them as one who tests them.

﴿Because they were defiantly disobedient﴾: that is, because of their continuous immorality, which has become their nature.

Some of them said: What Allah the Exalted related was nothing but like the condition of the Islamists of our time, in the gathering of all kinds of carnal enjoyments of foods, drinks, amusements, and marriages, openly in the markets and gatherings, on the honored days such as the festivals and the blessed times, such as the times of visiting the shrines of the righteous, which are well known and famous among the people.

﴿And when a community from among them said﴾, and they are the heart and its followers, to the admonishing community, which is the spirit and its followers: ﴿Why do you admonish a people﴾, and they are the commanding self and its powers?

﴿Allah will destroy them or punish them with a severe punishment﴾
[Page 110]
for their deeds? ﴿They said: as an excuse﴾ before your Lord; that is, we admonish them as an excuse before Him, the Exalted; and that is because we were created to enjoin good and forbid evil, so we want to fulfill what is incumbent upon us, so that it may be manifest that we have not changed from our attributes.

﴿And perhaps they will fear Allah﴾, for they are receptive to this by their natural disposition, so we do not despair of their piety.

﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾, due to the dominance of wretchedness over them.

﴿We saved those who forbade evil﴾, and they are the spirit, the heart, and their followers, for they all forbade that, except that some of them grew weary, while some did not.

﴿And We seized those who wronged with a wretched punishment﴾: that is, severe; and it is the punishment of being deprived of receiving the outpouring (fayd).

﴿For what they had been defiantly disobedient﴾: that is, because of their persistence in going out of obedience.

﴿When they insolently refused what they had been forbidden﴾: that is, they refused to abandon that, ﴿We said to them: Be apes, despised﴾: that is, We made their natures like their natures; and that is beyond being deprived of receiving the outpouring.

﴿And when your Lord proclaimed﴾: that is, swore an oath ﴿that He would surely send against them until the Day of Resurrection﴾, that is, their resurrection, ﴿someone who would afflict them﴾, and that is the majestic manifestation (al-tajalli al-jalali), ﴿with the worst torment﴾, and that is the punishment of subjugation and the humiliation of following desires, ﴿And We divided them﴾: that is, We scattered the Children of Israel, the spirit, ﴿throughout the earth﴾: that is, the earth of the body, ﴿in nations﴾, groups; ﴿among them are the righteous﴾, that is, those perfect in righteousness, like the intellect; ﴿and among them are those below that﴾ in it, like the heart; and whoever makes the heart more perfect than the intellect has reversed the matter; ﴿And We tested them with good and evil﴾, the manifestations of beauty and majesty; ﴿so that perhaps they would return﴾ by annihilation (fana') to Us. ﴿Then there succeeded them a successor﴾, and that is the self and its powers, ﴿who inherited the Book﴾, and that is what Allah the Exalted inspired into the intellect and the heart; ﴿they take the goods of this lower life﴾, and that is the base desires and the perishing pleasures, and they make what they inherited a means (dhari'ah) to take that; ﴿and they say: It will be forgiven us﴾, and there is no doubt, for we will reach (wasilun) and be perfected; and this is the state of many of the Sufis of our time; for they throw themselves at desires like the moth into the fire, and they say: That will not harm us, for we have reached.

It is related from some of them that he eats pure ḥarām, and says: The affirmation and negation (of the Shahada) repels its harm. This is a gross error and clear misguidance; may Allah the Exalted protect us and you from that. Greater than that is the belief in the permissibility of eating the like of carrion without a legal excuse, for one of them says: Each of us is a sea, and the sea is not made impure. This misguided one does not realize that whoever believes this is more impure than the dog and the pig. Among them is one who relates from some of the perfect, accomplished people of Allah the Exalted what supports his claim, and it is such-and-such, which has no basis; and far be it, far be it, that that perfect one should be associated with what is attributed to him.

﴿And if they come to them with any goods like it, they will take it﴾: that is, they are persistent in this ugly deed.

﴿Was not the covenant of the Book taken from them﴾, which is recorded in what Allah the Exalted inspired into the intellect and the heart, ﴿that they should not say about Allah except the truth﴾? So how did they deviate from it? ﴿And they studied what is in it﴾, of what contains their guidance; ﴿and the Last Abode﴾, which comprises spiritual pleasures, ﴿is better for those who fear Allah﴾, [who reject] this lower life. ﴿And those who hold fast to the Book﴾: that is, who cling to what Allah the Exalted inspired into the intellect and the heart of wisdoms and knowledge; ﴿and establish the prayer﴾ and spare no effort in obedience; ﴿Indeed, We do not waste the reward of the righteous﴾ among them, and their reward varies according to the degree of their righteousness, until it reaches what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.

﴿And when We raised the mountain over them﴾, and it is the mountain of the Lordly command and the divine subjugation, ﴿as though it were a canopy﴾, a great cloud; ﴿and they thought it would fall upon them﴾ if they did not accept the rulings of Allah, glorified is He; ﴿Take what We have given you with strength﴾, with earnestness and resolve; ﴿and remember what is in it﴾ of the secrets; ﴿that perhaps you may fear Allah﴾, that you may be counted among the ranks of the God-fearing, according to the differences in the levels of their piety.

The discussion of His, glorified is He, statement: ﴿And when your Lord took...﴾ and so on, belongs to this category; what we have mentioned in the course of its interpretation from the words of the people of Allah, may Allah sanctify their secrets, suffices in place of it. Except that some of them mention that the first atom that answered "Yes" (bala) was the atom of the Prophet (ﷺ). Likewise,
[Page 111]
it is the first to respond from the earth when Allah, glorified is He, addressed the heavens and the earth, saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Come willingly or unwillingly.﴾ They said: ﴿We come willingly.﴾ It was from the dust of the Ka'bah, and it is the first thing created from the earth, and from it the earth was spread out, as related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both. This would imply that his burial, (ﷺ), should be in Mecca, where his noble dust came from.

And they have related that a person is buried where his dust was.

But it was said: when the water surged, it cast the foam to the sides, and the atom of the Prophet (ﷺ) fell to what lies opposite his noble tomb in Medina. It may be inferred from this statement that he, peace and blessings be upon him, is the origin of creation, and that the existents are subordinate to him, (ﷺ). It was said:

And because his atom is the mother of creation, he was called "unlettered" (ummi). Some of them mentioned that the letter "ba'" is because it is the first letter with which the atom opened its mouth when it spoke. The children in this world have not ceased to pronounce it at the beginning of their lives, and this is no wonder, for every child is born upon the fitrah. It was said: And because of the greatness of the secrets Allah, glorified and exalted is He, placed in the letter "ba'", Allah began His Book with it, indeed He began every surah with it, because of the precedence of the basmalah, which begins with it, over every surah except al-Tawbah; and the opening of that is with Bara'ah, whose first letter is also "ba'". And because the hamzah, which is called alif, was the first letter that struck their ears in that scene, it was the first of the letters, but it did not appear in the basmalah at the beginning of the Book, for a secret we have alluded to. And Allah, the Exalted, is the Guide to the right path of correctness.

﴿And recite to them﴾ is conjoined to the implicit verb governing "when He took" (﴿إذ أخذ﴾). It follows the pattern of reporting a reversal after a turn of events. That is, "And recite to the Jews, or to your people, as in al-Khazin," ﴿the news of him to whom We gave Our signs﴾, meaning his report, which has significance and importance. As Ibn Mardawayh and others narrated through several chains from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, he was Bal'am ibn Ba'ura' (Bal'am son of Ba'ura'). In another wording, he was Bil'am ibn Ba'ir. He was from the Canaanites. In a narration from Ibn 'Abbas and Abu Talha, he was from the Children of Israel. Ibn 'Asakir narrated from Ibn Shihab that he was Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Habr (Ibn 'Abbas) that he was a man from the Children of Israel who had a wife called al-Basus. In another narration, which Ibn Hatim transmitted from him, he was al-Nu'man ibn Sayfi al-Rahib (the monk). That he was an Israelite is more fitting to the context, as is clear. The most well-known view is that he was Bal'am or Bal'am. He had been given knowledge of some of the Books of Allah, the Exalted. Less famous is the view that he was Umayya, and that he had read some of the books.

﴿Then he detached himself from them﴾, that is, from those signs, like the detaching of the skin from the sheep. The meaning is that he went out from them entirely, by disbelieving in them and casting them behind his back. The literal meaning of salkh (stripping) is peeling off the skin and removing it completely from what it covers. It is said of anything that separates from something in the most complete manner: "he detached himself from it" (insalakha minhu). In using this expression there is an emphasis that is not hidden. Some scholars drew evidence from this verse that knowledge is not removed from men, since He, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿Then he detached himself from them﴾ and did not say, may His majesty be exalted: "then it detached itself from him."

﴿So Satan overtook him﴾, that is, he caught up with him and reached him, as al-Raghib said, after he had not been reaching him because of his precedence in faith and obedience. Al-Jawhari said: "It is said: atba'tu al-qawm (I made the people follow), when they have preceded you and you catch up with them." The meaning seems to be: I made them followers of me after I had been a follower of them. In this there is then an emphasis on overtaking, since he is made as if he were an imam (leader) for Satan, and Satan follows him. This is among the blameworthy, and a parallel to this is the saying of the poet:

A youth was among the army of Iblis, until his state rose with him so that Iblis became one of his army.

Some scholars stated that its meaning is istatba'ahu (he made him follow), that is, he made him a follower of himself. It is said that this is transitive to two objects, the second of which is omitted, meaning: he made him follow his steps. It was read: (fa-ittaba'ahu), from the form ifti'al (meaning he followed him willingly).

﴿So he became of the misguided﴾, that is, he became one of the group of the astray who are firmly rooted in error, after he had been guided. The manner of this, according to the view that he was Bal'am, is that when Musa, peace be upon him, intended to fight the giants, the people of Bal'am came to him. He had with him the Greatest Name of Allah, the Exalted. They said to him: "Musa, peace be upon him, is a formidable man, and with him are many soldiers, and he has come to drive us out of our land, so pray to Allah, the Exalted, that He turn him back from us." He said: "Woe to you! He is the Prophet of Allah, the Exalted, and with him are the angels and the believers. How can I pray against them, when I know of Allah, the Exalted, what I know, and if I do so my world and my hereafter will perish?" They insisted upon him. He said: "Until I consult my Lord." He was shown in a dream and it was said to him: "Do not do it." He informed his people, and they gave him a gift, and he accepted it. They did not cease humbling themselves before him until they tempted him. He began to pray against Musa, peace and blessings be upon him, and his people. But Allah, the Exalted, kept turning his tongue to pray against his own people. They said: "O Bal'am, do you know what you are doing? You are praying against us!" He said: "This is a matter in which Allah, the Exalted, has overpowered me." His tongue hung out and fell upon his chest. He said: "O people, both the world and the hereafter have gone from me, and nothing remains but cunning and stratagem. Adorn the women, send them out, and order them not to refuse themselves, for the people are travelers, and Allah, glorified and exalted, hates adultery. If they fall into it, they will perish." They did that, and Zimri ibn Shalum, the chief of the tribe of Shim'un, son of Ya'qub, was tempted by a woman from among them called Kasti daughter of Sur. Musa, peace be upon him, forbade him from the immorality, but he refused and brought her into his tent and committed adultery with her. Plague then fell upon them, until seventy thousand of them died. It did not lift until Phinehas ibn al-'Izar ibn Harun killed the two of them, and he had been absent at the beginning of the matter.

On the authority of Muqatil: the king of al-Balqa' said to him: "Pray to Allah, the Exalted, against Musa, peace be upon him." He said: "He is of my religion, and I will not pray against him." So the king set up a wooden cross for him to crucify him on. He prayed with the Greatest Name that Allah, the Exalted, not let Musa, peace be upon him, enter the city. This was granted to him, and the Children of Israel fell into the wandering (al-tih). Musa said: "My Lord, for what sin is this?" He, glorified and exalted, said: "Because of the prayer of Bal'am." He said: "My Lord, as You heard his prayer against me, hear my prayer against him." So he prayed to Allah, may His majesty be exalted, that He remove from him the Greatest Name and faith. Allah, the Exalted, removed from him the knowledge and stripped him of it, and it came out of his chest like a white dove.

This is refuted by saying that the wandering was a repose and comfort for Musa, peace be upon him, and the Children of Israel were only punished by it. That occurred by his prayer, peace be upon him. Moreover, there is discussion regarding a prayer for the removal of faith. I am amazed why this wretched one did not pray with the Greatest Name that he knew against the king of al-Balqa', to save himself from his evil. And his praying against Musa, peace be upon him, is nothing but black ignorance.

It has come in the words of Abu al-Mu'tamir that he had been given prophethood. This is refuted by the fact that the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them, cannot be subject to disbelief according to any sensible person. It seems his meaning of prophethood is what he was given of the signs. This is like the saying of the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever memorizes the Qur'an has folded prophethood between his two sides."

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Malik ibn Dinar that he was one of the scholars of the Children of Israel. Musa, peace be upon him, used to advance him in hardships, and disliked him, and favored him. So he sent him to the king of Madyan, calling them to Allah, the Exalted. He was one whose supplication was answered. So he abandoned the religion of Musa, peace be upon him, and followed the religion of the king. This narration, in my view, is more worthy of acceptance than what came before.

As for the view that he was Umayya, he had read the ancient books and knew that Allah, the Exalted, would send a messenger. He hoped that he would be that messenger. It happened that he went out to al-Bahrayn, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, received prophethood. He remained there for eight years, then came back and met the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, in a group of his companions. He called him to Islam and recited to him Surat Ya-Sin. When he had finished it, Umayya leapt up dragging his legs. Quraysh followed him saying: "What are you saying, O Umayya?" He said: "I testify that he is upon the truth." They said: "Shall we follow him?" He said: "Until I look into his matter." He went out to al-Sham. He came back after the Battle of Badr intending to embrace Islam. When he was informed of it (the Muslim victory), he abandoned Islam and said: "If he were a prophet, he would not have killed his own kin." He went to al-Ta'if

[Page 113]

and died there. His sister al-Fari'a came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, and he asked her about his death. She mentioned to him that at his death he recited:

Every life, however long it lasts for a time, will eventually pass away.

Would that I had been, before what has become clear to me, grazing the wild goats on the peaks of the mountains.

Indeed the Day of Reckoning is a great day, in which the small becomes gray, a heavy day.

Then he, peace and blessings be upon him, said to her: "Recite to me some of your brother's poetry." She recited to him:

To You is all praise, and blessing, and grace, our Lord, and nothing is higher than You in majesty and glory.

The King over the throne of heaven, the Guardian, before whose might faces bow down and prostrate.

From a long qasida which she completed to its end. Then she recited to him his qasida in which he says:

The people stood for the reckoning all together, so one is wretched and punished, and one is happy.

And in which:

Before the Lord of the Throne they are presented, He who knows the loud and the secret hidden.

The Day the Merciful comes, and He is Merciful; indeed His promise is certain to come.

My Lord, if You pardon, pardon is my hope; or if You punish, You do not punish the innocent.

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Indeed your brother's poetry believed, but his heart disbelieved." And Allah, the Exalted, revealed the verse.

As for the view that he was al-Nu'man, he had become a monk in the time of ignorance and wore woolen garments. He came to Madina and said to the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him: "What is this that you have brought?" The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The hanifiyya (primordial monotheism), the religion of Ibrahim, peace be upon him." He said: "I am upon it." The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "You are not upon it, but you have introduced into it what is not part of it." He said: "May Allah cause the liar among us to die, a wanderer, alone." Then he went out to al-Sham and sent to the hypocrites: "Prepare your weapons." Then he came to Caesar and asked him for troops to drive the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, out of Madina. He died in al-Sham, a wanderer, alone.

As for the view that he was the husband of al-Basus, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he was a man who was given three answered supplications. He had a wife called al-Basus, and he had a son by her. She said: "Make one of them for me." He said: "What is it that you want?" She said: "Pray to Allah, the Exalted, that He make me the most beautiful woman among the Children of Israel." He prayed to Allah, the Exalted, and He made her the most beautiful woman among them. When she knew that there was no one among them like her, she turned away from him and desired something else. He prayed to Allah, the Exalted, that He make her a female dog, and she became a female dog. Two supplications went. Her sons came and said: "We cannot remain in this state; our mother has become a female dog, and people taunt us with her. Pray to Allah that He return her to the state she was in." He prayed, and she returned as she had been. The three supplications were gone in her. From here it is said: "More ill-omened than al-Basus." This is a name for that man, and it is nothing. This narration is not supported by the structure of the Noble Qur'an, as is not hidden. What we know is that al-Basus, by whom a proverb is coined, is the daughter of Munqidh al-Tamimiyya, the maternal aunt of Jassas ibn Murra ibn Dhuhl al-Shaybani, the slayer of Kulayb. Her story is long, and al-Maydani and others have mentioned it.

[Page 114]

It is narrated from al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan that the intended one to whom the signs were given, and who detached himself from them, were the hypocrites among the People of the Book, who used to know the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, as they know their own sons, but did not believe in him, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, with a true faith. This is far-fetched because of the singular form of the relative pronoun. It is narrated from Qatada that this is a parable for one to whom guidance was presented, and who was prepared for it, but turned away from it and refused to accept it. This contains contradictions to the well-known narrations. The weakest of the views in my opinion is the view of Abu Muslim: that the intended one is Pharaoh, and the intended signs are the proofs and miracles indicating the truthfulness of Musa, peace be upon him. It is as if it were said: "And recite to them the news of Pharaoh, when We gave him the proofs indicating the truthfulness of Musa, peace be upon him, but he did not accept them."

Page 115

Allah's words, ﴿Had We willed, We would have elevated him thereby﴾, form a new sentence (*kalam mustanaf*) brought in to explain what was mentioned about the *inslakh* (the shedding or stripping away of the signs) and what follows from it. The pronoun in *rafa'nahu* ("We would have elevated him") refers to the one who was given the signs, and the pronoun in *bihā* ("thereby") refers to the signs. The *bā'* is causal (*sababiyyah*). The object of the verb of willing is omitted, and it is the content of the conditional clause, as is the established rule. The meaning is: Had We willed to elevate him, We would have raised him to the ranks of the righteous, because of those signs and his acting upon what they contain. It has also been said that the object pronoun refers to disbelief (*kufr*), which is understood from the preceding discourse. The meaning would then be: Had We willed, We would have removed disbelief through the signs. In this reading, *al-raf'* (elevation) comes from the expression "the injustice was lifted from us" (*rufi'a al-zulm 'anna*). This reading is very far from the apparent meaning, even though it is reported from Mujahid. Even further from the apparent meaning, and more remote still, is what is reported from al-Balkhi and al-Zajjaj, who made the pronoun *bihā* refer to disobedience (*al-ma'siyah*).

﴿But he clung to the earth﴾ means he inclined to this world and was drawn to it. This is how al-Suddi and Ibn Jubayr interpreted it. The root meaning of *al-ikhlad* (clinging, adhering) is remaining in a place, from *al-khulud* (eternity). Because this involves inclination, it was interpreted in this way. The earth is interpreted as the world because it contains its pleasures and everything sought from it.

Al-Raghib said: The meaning is that he settled upon the earth, thinking that he would remain in it forever. Several scholars interpreted "the earth" as lowliness (*al-sifalah*).

﴿and followed his desire﴾, in preferring this world, and turned away from what those noble signs required. In the connection of the elevation with the will, followed by the turn away from it to the servant's act, there is an indication, as Nasir al-Din said: The will is a cause of the act that leads to elevation. The absence of elevation is evidence of the absence of the will, by the principle that the absence of an effect shows the absence of its cause. The true cause is the will, and what we observe of causes are intermediary means that are considered in the realization of the effect, insofar as the will has been connected to it in that manner. As he said, it should have been stated: "but he turned away from them." Instead, what was mentioned was placed in its position for emphasis, because it is a *kinayah* (allusion or metonymy), which is more eloquent than explicit statement. It also serves to point to what drove him to it, and that the love of this world is the root of every sin. How delicate is the attribution of the coming of the signs and the elevation to Allah, and the attribution of the shedding and the clinging to the servant, even though everything is from Allah, the Exalted. In this there is teaching the servants the good manners it contains. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, goodness is in Your hands, and evil is not attributed to You."

Al-Zamakhshari, when he saw that the apparent meaning of the verse contradicts his doctrine, since it indicates that all existing things occur by the will of Allah, the Exalted, resorted to *ta'wil* (figurative interpretation). He made the will a *majaz* (figurative usage) for its cause, which is the servant's adherence to the signs, by the indication of the contrast with the servant's act, which is the opposite of adhering to the signs, namely clinging to the earth. The meaning is: Had he adhered to them, We would have elevated him. This is of the type of removing the shoe before reaching the water, and of resorting to figurative meaning before its time, since it is possible that "Had We willed" remains on its literal meaning, and "he clung to the earth" is a figurative expression for its cause, which is the absence of the will to elevate him, rather than the clinging. He did not rely on his crutch, because the antithesis would be lost in that case. In *al-Kashf* it is said that interpreting the will as the cause of what it causes, according to his claim, is no more preferable than interpreting the clinging as the cause of what it causes, according to our claim. How so, when the words of the Glorified and Exalted, ﴿Had We willed﴾, are a contrast to His words ﴿and he shed them﴾? Moreover, clinging is inclination, and will, inclination and similar meanings are, by agreement, not acts of the servants. Yes, the firm resolve that accompanies an act is an act of the heart according to them. Then the words of the Glorified and Exalted, ﴿Whom Allah guides﴾, and His words, ﴿And We have certainly created﴾, confirm what the People of the Sunnah hold with the strongest confirmation. But al-Zamakhshari does not pay attention to this.

﴿So his likeness is that of the dog﴾, which is the well-known animal. Its plurals are *aklub*, *kilab* and *kilabat*, as Ibn Sida said, and *kulayb*, on the pattern of *'ubayd*, which is rare. *Aklub* is also pluralized as *akalib*. It is used as a proverb for baseness, because it eats excrement and returns to its vomit, and carrion is dearer to it than fresh meat. Yes, and it is better than an evil man. Among what is attributed to al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him:

Would that the dogs were our neighbors, and that we did not see anyone among those we see.

Indeed the dogs rest quietly in their resting places, while people are never quiet; their evil never ceases.

In *Shu'ab al-Iman* by al-Bayhaqi, from the jurist Mansur, it is reported that he used to recite for himself:

The dog is the best of companions, and yet it is the extreme of baseness,

[compared to] one who disputes over leadership before the times of leadership.

The *mathal* (likeness) here means the attribute, as several scholars said. So its attribute is like the attribute of the dog. It has also been said that the meaning is that he is like the dog in lowliness.

﴿If you pursue him﴾, that is, if you press upon him and chase him away, ﴿he pants﴾.

﴿Or if you leave him﴾ in his state, ﴿he pants﴾, that is, he is constantly panting in every condition. *Al-lahath* (panting) is the protrusion of the tongue with a strong breath. This is a natural trait of the dog, which cannot easily expel warm air and draw in cool air, because of the weakness of its heart and the failing of its heart's action. Other animals are different: they do not need strong breathing, and distress and constriction only affect them when they are tired and exhausted.

The choice of the nominal sentence over the verbal one, by saying "so his likeness becomes like the likeness of..." etc., indicates the continuity of his being characterized by that base state and the complete persistence of his remaining in it. The address in the two conditional verbs is to everyone who has a share of being addressed, because this makes more widespread the horror of his condition. It has been said that the two conditional clauses have no place in grammatical parsing (*i'rab*), because they are an elaboration of what was summarized in the example, and an explanation of what was left vague in it, specifying the aspect of resemblance. This follows the pattern of His words, ﴿He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he is﴾, after His words, ﴿Indeed the likeness of Jesus with Allah is like the likeness of Adam﴾ (peace be upon them). It has also been said that they are in the accusative position as a *hal* (circumstantial clause) of the dog, based on their being transformed into the sense of equality (*taswiyah*), just as the interrogative was transformed into this sense in His words, ﴿It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them﴾. As if it was said: panting in both states. A conditional clause, as we have previously mentioned, may occur as a circumstantial clause in general. The author of *al-Diya'* said that it hardly occurs as such in its entirety. Rather, when it is intended to occur as a circumstantial clause, it is made a predicate of the circumstantial element, as in: "Zayd came to me," and "He is, if you ask him, he gives you." Thus one makes it a nominal sentence with the *waw*, because the conditional particle, due to its initial position, hardly connects to what precedes it unless there is an added force. Yes, if you remove it from its literal meaning, it is permissible, whether its opposite is conjoined to it, in which case the *waw* must be dropped, as in our present case, or it is not conjoined, in which case the *waw* is required so that it is not confused with the true conditional, as in: "I will come to you even if you do not come to me."

The comparison has been said to be a comparison of single things with single things. It has also been said, and many verifiers hold this, that it is a comparison of a state (*hay'ah*) abstracted from what he suffered after the shedding: bad condition, burning of the heart, constant anxiety and restlessness, and no rest in any state. This state is abstracted from what was mentioned in the case of the dog. It has been reported, and we have already pointed to it earlier, that when Bal'am supplicated against Musa (peace be upon him), his tongue came out and hung over his chest, and he began panting like a dog until he died. So the point of resemblance is either intellectual or sensory.

﴿That﴾ is a reference to the attribute of the dog, or to the one who shed the signs. The demonstrative indicates distance, as has passed more than once.

Page 116

﴿The likeness of the people who denied Our signs﴾. It is intended, as reported from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, to be the people of Makkah. They used to wish for a guide to guide them and a caller to call them to obedience to Allah, the Exalted. Then when there came to them one whose truthfulness and trustworthiness they did not doubt, they denied him and turned away from the signs, and did not believe in them. Or it is intended to be the Jews, as several scholars said, since they read the description of the Prophet (ﷺ) in the Torah, and the Torah mentioned the Qur'an, which is a miracle, and what it contains. So they affirmed him, gave good news to the people of the nearness of his mission, and used to seek victory through him. But when there came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it, and so they shed the ruling of the Torah. Or it is the more general, including both these and those, and everyone who is characterized by this description, as in al-Khazin. I say this, and the Jews enter into this primarily.

﴿So relate the stories﴾. *Al-qasas* (the stories) is a verbal noun used to name the object, as in *al-salb* (the spoil). The definite article in it is for previous reference (*'ahd*). The *fa'* indicates that what follows is a consequence of what precedes it, meaning: when it is established that the mentioned likeness is the likeness of these deniers, then relate that to them.

﴿That perhaps they may reflect﴾, so that they may be restrained from what they are upon of disbelief and error. The clause is either in the position of a circumstantial element from the pronoun of the addressee, or in the position of a object of purpose. The meaning is: relate, hoping for their reflection, or in hope of their reflection.

﴿Evil is the example﴾ is a resumptive clause (isti'naf, a new sentence) that comes to show the full ugliness of those who deny, after the preceding clarification. *Sa'a* here has the meaning of *bi'sa* (what an evil thing), its subject (fa'il) is an implied pronoun, and *mathalan* is a specifying accusative (tamyiz, a noun that specifies the vagueness of the verb) that explains that pronoun. The specifying accusative may be made masculine, pluralized, or otherwise inflected without changing the verb's pronoun, and its original form is to be transitive to one object. The thing praised or censured (al-mukhassas bil-dhamm) is His saying, glorified and exalted be He: ﴿the people who denied Our signs﴾. Since the subject, the specifying accusative and the thing censured must all refer to one and the same thing, while *mathal* (example) is distinct from *al-qawm* (the people), it becomes necessary to posit an omitted element, either in the thing censured, which is the apparent reading, or in the specifying accusative. That is: "Evil is the example, the example of the people," or "Evil is the people, the example of the people."

In the Hawashi al-Shihabiyya it is stated that it has been read with *mathal* in the genitive construction with two fathas, and *mithl* with a kasra and sukun, both governed by *lil-qawm* and in the nominative with *sa'a* as an expression of wonder. Its estimated form is on the pattern of a verb with a damma, like *qada'a al-rajul* (the man was excellent), and *mathalu al-qawm* is the subject (fa'il), meaning: how wicked they are! The relative clause is then in the genitive position as an attribute of *al-qawm*, or it has the meaning of *bi'sa* and *mathalu* is the subject, while the relative clause is itself the thing censured in the nominative position, with an omitted genitive noun, meaning: the example of those who, etc.

Abu Hayyan estimated a specifying accusative in this reading, but al-Samin rejected this, saying that it is not needed for the specifying accusative when the subject is explicit, to the point that they made the combining of the two a matter of necessity. There are three positions on this: prohibition in all cases, permission in all cases, and a distinction: if the two are distinct it is permitted, as in *ni'ma al-rajulu shuja'an Zaydun* (what an excellent man is Zayd, in bravery), and otherwise it is not permitted. Some make the thing censured an omitted element, and there is disagreement about what it is. Repeating *al-qawm* described by the relative clause, while the pronoun would suffice, as in saying *sa'a mathalan mathaluhum* (evil is the example, their example), serves to notify that the root of the evil lies in what is within the scope of the relative clause. It also links His saying, glorified and exalted be He: ﴿and they were wronging themselves﴾ to it. This is either coordinated with *kadhdhabu* (they denied), and thus falls within the same scope of the relative clause, meaning they combined two foul matters, denial and wronging themselves in particular; or it is disconnected from it, meaning: they did not wrong anyone except themselves, for its harm does not go beyond them. Whichever it is, this contains an allusion to the fact that their denial of the signs includes wronging them, and that this is also taken into account in the restriction derived from the fronting (of the object). Al-Tibi, al-Qutb and others have stated that, on the reading of disconnection, the sentence is a concluding and emphatic statement to the sentence before it. The words of some of them suggest that the fronting of the object in the first reading is for the sake of the rhyme (fasila), and in the second reading is to indicate restriction, and that the cause of their wronging themselves is the denial. There is obscurity in this, as is not hidden.

Then, these verses are among those that strike the scholars of evil with the third of the stones of the hearth (a proverb for the utmost calamity). Our master al-Tibi, may God make his resting place pure, has mentioned that whoever reflects on this example and the rest of the examples struck in the revelation regarding the polytheists and the idols, such as the spider's house and the fly, will realize that the scholars of evil are worse and more repugnant than that. How wretched is the example that is applied to them, and what they are engaged in of eagerness for the world, its wealth and its status, and their inclining toward its pleasures and desires, from following the commanding soul and loosening its reins in its aims. May God Most High protect us and the Muslims from that.

It is related from our master Shaykh al-Islam Shihab al-Din al-Suhrawardi that he wrote to the Imam Fakhr al-Din al-Razi, may God cover them both with His good pleasure, regarding the determination in the age for the dissemination of knowledge, whose blessing God Most High has magnified for him: it is fitting for the vigilant and skilled among the masters of religion to support him with good supplication, so that God Most High may purify the source of his knowledge of the realities of piety and its origin from the impurities of desire, for a drop of desire clouds a sea of knowledge. The impulses of desire that are implanted in souls, which accompany it from its origin in the lower world, when they mix with knowledge, they lower it in several ways; and when the sources and springs of knowledge are clear of desire, the words of God Most High sustain it, which the sea would be exhausted before they are exhausted, and knowledge remains in its full strength. This is the rank of those firmly grounded in knowledge, not of those who merely display it. They are the heirs of the prophets, peace be upon them. Their action follows their knowledge, and knowledge and action alternate in them, until their deeds become pure and subtle and become secret conversations and spiritual dialogues. Deeds take the form of knowledge because of their subtlety, and knowledge takes the form of deeds because of the strength of their action and their spread into capacities. In following desire there is an inclination toward the earth, as God Most High said: ﴿Had We willed, We would have raised him thereby, but he clung to the earth and followed his desire﴾. So the purification of the light of thought from the vile fancies and from being held captive by illusions, which have bequeathed small minds, and the flattery of inferior souls, is a matter for mature men. Thus their pure souls accompany the Higher Assembly and roam in the fields of holiness. Freedom from the trial of the world's debris, and fleeing from seeking the approval of the gaze and beliefs of creation, these are the places where illnesses are overcome. The seeker of the Supreme Companion is one who is spoken to and addressed. The divine disclosures come upon him because of his knowledge of the form of trial, and his eradication of its root through sincere reliance on God, the frequency of his entry into the sanctuary of divine nearness, and his immersion with every breath in the seas of the eye of certainty, and his washing away the spittle of the proofs of demonstration with the light of direct vision. Thus demonstration is for thoughts, not for secrets, to the end of what he said. How wondrous is this admonition of a wise man and advice of a sincere friend! We ask God Most High to guide us to what it has pointed to.

﴿Whomever Allah guides, he is the one who is guided; and whomever He leads astray, those are the losers.﴾ This is a concluding statement (*tadhyil*) that confirms what the preceding story contained, in line with what some of them have said. Another scholar said: when Allah, exalted is He, commanded His Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to relate to those astray the story of their brother so that they might reflect and abandon what they are upon, He then established after that that guidance and misguidance come from Him, glory be to Him and exalted is He, and that admonition and reminder are only among the ordinary means (*al-wasa'it al-'adiyya*) in the attainment of guidance, because they are incitements that turn the responsible person (*al-mukallaf*) by his choice toward obtaining it, in accordance with what Allah, exalted is He, has attached His creation of him to. The intended guidance here is that which necessarily produces being guided, certainly. This is not because its reality is the indication that conveys one to the desired goal, as the words of some of our companions seem to imply. Rather, it is because it is the complete instance (*al-fard al-kamil*) of the reality of guidance, which is indication toward what leads to the goal. This is shown by its attribution to Allah, exalted is He, by the fact that being guided is made a consequence of it, and by its being contrasted with misguidance and what goes with it. It is not hidden that guidance in this sense necessarily entails being guided. Thus the informing of the guidance of the one whom Allah has guided is, as has been said, in the manner of the expression "my poetry, my poetry" (*shi'ri shi'ri*). It conveys the magnification of the status of being guided, that it is in itself a great perfection and a mighty benefit, and that it suffices for attaining every honor in this world and the next.

Some of the verifying scholars (*al-muhaqqiqin*) have chosen that the intended meaning is not merely the informing of what has been mentioned, lest one suppose that it conveys nothing according to its outward sense and so be led to interpret it accordingly. Rather, it is the restriction of being guided to the one whom Allah, exalted is He, has guided, as the definite form of the predicate (*ta'rif al-khabar*) requires. So the meaning is: whoever Allah creates guidance in, he is the one who is guided, and none other, whoever he may be. This is not devoid of beauty. Yet it may be said that the first (interpretation) is more fitting to the contrast, and that the singular "the one guided" is in observance of the wording of "whoever" (*man*), while the plural "the losers" is in observance of its meaning, to signal that the truth is one while the paths of misguidance are many. The verse also explicitly states that guidance and misguidance are from Allah, exalted is He. So glory be to Him who misguided the Mu'tazila (*al-Mu'tazila*).

[Page 119]

﴿And We have certainly created﴾: this is an independent clause that confirms the content of what precedes it by way of a concluding statement (tadhyil). Dhara'a with a hamza means to create, and Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father) and others explained it so. That is, by Allah, the Exalted, We have certainly created ﴿for Hell many of the jinn and humankind﴾, and they are those who persist in disbelief according to His knowledge, glorified and exalted is He. The lam here is, according to most scholars, the lam of consequence (lam al-'aqiba), as in His words, exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, You have indeed given Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment and wealth in the life of this world. Our Lord, that they may lead astray from Your way﴾, and as in the words of the poet:

*For him there is an angel calling every day: "Give birth for death, and build for ruin."*

In al-Kashshaf it is said that they were made (for Hell) because of their deep immersion in disbelief and their intense obstinacy in it, and that only the deeds of the people of the Fire can proceed from them, so they were created for the Fire, indicating their complete immersion in the things that necessitate it and their firm establishment in what qualifies them to enter it. He also pointed out that this is a concluding statement (tadhyil) to the story of the Jews, after enumerating their ugly deeds, as a consolation to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It is as if it were said: "Among those whom warning does not benefit, leave them and concern yourself with your own affair, and with those who are upon your religion in adhering to monotheism." According to what he said, the verse is an instance of implicit allusion (kinaya ima'iyya) in the view of al-Qutb (may his secret be sanctified). His words imply that what prompted al-Zamakhshari to this interpretation is that if the apparent meaning is intended, it would necessitate that disbelief is what Allah wills, and this contradicts his school of thought. You know that most of the Ahl al-Sunna have interpreted the verse by taking the lam in the sense you have learned, due to His words, exalted is He: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and humankind except that they should worship Me﴾. For the explanation of creation by worship contradicts its explanation by Hell and entering it. Yes, Ibn 'Atiyya from among us went to the apparent meaning and taking the lam as causal. Some people claimed that the interpretation contradicts the hadiths narrated on this subject, such as some of the hadiths previously cited concerning the verse of the covenant, and what Imam Ahmad recorded in his Musnad from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Qatada, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah, the Exalted, created Adam (peace be upon him), then took out the creation from his back and said: 'These are for Paradise and I do not mind; and these are for the Fire and I do not mind.' Someone said: 'Then upon what is the action based?' He said: 'Upon conformity with the decree.'"

And what Muhyi al-Sunna recorded from 'A'isha, the Mother of the Believers (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) passed by the funeral of a child from the children of the Ansar, and I said: "O Messenger of Allah, good tidings for him, a bird from the birds of Paradise!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "And what would make you know? Indeed Allah created Paradise and created for it its people while they were in their fathers' loins, and He created the Fire and created for it its people while they were in their fathers' loins." And other than that.

Al-Tibi went to this view and supported it with what he supported it with, and claimed that the benefit of the oath is to alert to the uprooting of the doubts of whoever may take upon himself to interpret the verse and distort the decisive text. It is also reported from the Imam (al-Razi) that the verse is a proof for the soundness of the position of the Ahl al-Sunna regarding the question of the creation of actions and the will of created beings, because He, glorified and exalted is He, explicitly stated that He, majestic and exalted, created many of the jinn and humankind for Hell, and there is no further clarification from Allah, exalted is He. It is not hidden that taking the verse in its apparent meaning contradicts the apparent meaning of the verse we have mentioned, and in the Noble Book there is much that agrees with it. The true causality of His actions is, according to the well-known position, denied by Imam al-Ash'ari and his companions.

Some of the eminent scholars said: The intended "many" are those for whom the eternal word of wretchedness has been decreed, but not by way of compulsion (jabr), without it being from them anything that leads to that.
